techStack: Express v5, TypeScript ~6.0, ESM modules; middleware signature is standard (req, res, next)
No third-party rate-limiting library — hand-rolled in-memory Map<string, number[]>
RateLimitError extends AppError; constructor takes retryAfterSeconds: number; errorHandler reads err.retryAfterSeconds and sets Retry-After header automatically
TypeScript strict mode: noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters — introduced variables must be used
Test runner: Vitest v4 with supertest for integration tests; pnpm test from src/benchmark-backend/
features: rateLimiter is applied globally in app.ts (before cors, body parsing, and routes) — runs on every request
Limit: MAX_REQUESTS=10, WINDOW_MS=60000; store is Map<string, number[]> keyed by IP
GET /health is registered inline in app.ts, intended to be exempt from rate limiting
products.test.ts mocks the rateLimiter entirely — product test suite is unaffected by any fix to rateLimiter.ts
rateLimiter.test.ts has 2 existing tests: (1) allows first 10 requests, (2) returns 429 with Retry-After header on request 11+; both must continue to pass
errorHandler sets res.setHeader('Retry-After', err.retryAfterSeconds) for RateLimitError — no change needed there
architecture: Middleware registration order in app.ts: requestId → rateLimiter → cors → express.json() → routes → errorHandler
Health check guard is the very first statement in rateLimiter — fires before getIp, before any store interaction
RateLimitError is defined in src/errors/index.ts; re-exported from src/types/errors.ts
The errorHandler (src/middleware/errorHandler.ts) handles RateLimitError specifically — no changes needed there
Only src/benchmark-backend/src/middleware/rateLimiter.ts is to be modified; no routes, error handlers, or test files change
edgeCases: Pruning must occur before the timestamps.length >= MAX_REQUESTS check — otherwise stale entries inflate the count and requests are wrongly rejected
Filter predicate must be t > now - WINDOW_MS (strictly greater) — a timestamp exactly at the boundary is expired and must be excluded
Retry-After computation uses pruned[0] (oldest remaining timestamp); pruned[0] is always defined when the limit branch is reached (pruned.length >= MAX_REQUESTS)
Math.ceil ensures Retry-After is always >= 1 even when pruned[0] is 59999ms old (remaining window is 1ms → ceil(0.001) = 1), preventing a 0 or negative value
The three fixes are logically independent but Bug 2 (Retry-After) correctness depends on Bug 1 (pruning) being applied first — pruned[0] must reflect only in-window timestamps
Health check fix (Bug 3) is fully independent — it returns before reaching pruning or Retry-After logic
Each IP's timestamp array is isolated in the Map — pruning one IP's array cannot affect another IP's quota

tasks.requirement: 3 — GET /health must always receive HTTP 200; exemption check must use req.path === '/health' (with the leading slash)
tasks.description: Change req.path === 'health' to req.path === '/health' on the health-check guard line in rateLimiter. This is the first statement in the middleware and is fully independent of the other two fixes.

tasks.requirement: 1 — All timestamps older than 60 seconds must be removed from the store before the count is compared against MAX_REQUESTS
tasks.description: After retrieving the timestamp array from the store (store.get(ip) ?? []), apply a filter to keep only entries where t > now - WINDOW_MS. Assign the result to a new variable (e.g. pruned) and use that variable for all subsequent operations (count check, store update, Retry-After computation). This must happen before the timestamps.length >= MAX_REQUESTS guard.

tasks.requirement: 2 — When a 429 is returned, the Retry-After header value must equal Math.ceil((timestamps[0] + WINDOW_MS - now) / 1000) where timestamps[0] is the oldest in-window timestamp after pruning
tasks.description: Replace const retryAfter = 60 with const retryAfter = Math.ceil((pruned[0] + WINDOW_MS - now) / 1000), where pruned is the filtered array from task-2. This value is passed into new RateLimitError(retryAfter) and flows through errorHandler to the Retry-After response header automatically.

tasks.requirement: 4 — All existing visible tests continue to pass without modification
tasks.description: After applying tasks 1–3, run pnpm test from src/benchmark-backend/ to confirm rateLimiter.test.ts and products.test.ts both exit with code 0. No test files are modified. The two rateLimiter tests (allow 10 requests, return 429 with Retry-After on 11th) must still pass; products tests are unaffected because they mock rateLimiter.
